title: Matching Linear, Exponential, and Quintic Functions y = 5x, y = 5^x, y = x^5 to Their Graphs
originalTopic: Theory and Examples: Function Families Comparison
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Match each equation (a) y = 5x, (b) y = 5^x, and (c) y = x^5 with its corresponding graph (f, g, or h), where g is a straight line through the origin, f is a strictly positive curve passing through (0, 1), and h is an S-shaped curve passing through the origin in Quadrants I and III.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } y = 5x \to g; \quad \text{(b) } y = 5^x \to f; \quad \text{(c) } y = x^5 \to h

steps.title: Identify the Linear Function y = 5x
steps.mathExpression: y = 5x \implies \text{Straight line through } (0, 0) \text{ with slope } 5 \to \text{Graph } g
steps.explanation: The equation y = 5x is a linear function whose graph is a straight line passing through the origin, which uniquely matches line g.
steps.why: Only a first-degree polynomial has a constant slope everywhere.

steps.title: Identify the Exponential Function y = 5^x
steps.explanation: The exponential function y = 5^x is strictly positive for all real x, passes through the y-intercept (0, 1), and approaches 0 as x -> -infinity. This uniquely matches curve f.
steps.why: An exponential function b^x (with b > 1) never crosses the x-axis and always passes through (0, 1).

steps.title: Identify the Quintic Power Function y = x^5
steps.mathExpression: y = x^5 \implies \text{Odd power curve through } (0, 0) \text{ in Quadrants I and III} \to \text{Graph } h
steps.explanation: The fifth-degree power function y = x^5 is an odd function that passes through the origin (0, 0) with a flat inflection tangent and extends into Quadrants I and III, matching curve h.
steps.why: Odd power functions x^n (n > 1) are nonlinear curves symmetric about the origin.
